limits: Phase between the two pathogenic alleles is unknown: no shared physical-phasing group, and no parental samples
No functional study was fetched in this run (no literature search), so PS3 is not claimed for either allele
Stage 4 (Exomiser) had not run in the recorded run, so no phenotype-rank record is cited
ClinVar assertions are interpretations of others' evidence, not observations on this proband
mechanism_hypothesis: Biallelic loss of CFTR function, if the alleles are in trans: p.Gly542Ter is a null allele, a premature stop predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay [vep:7:117587778:G:T], and p.Phe508del a folding-defective allele that is retained and degraded before reaching the apical membrane, with reduced channel gating in what does [vep:7:117559590:ATCT:A] [clinvar:VCV000007105]. A minimal-function plus F508del genotype, consistent with classic pancreatic-insufficient cystic fibrosis.
phase_statement: p.Phe508del is read-phased (PGT 1|0, PID 117559403_A_G) against two common alleles 76 and 111 bp upstream, so it is in trans to those; p.Gly542Ter, 28.2 kb downstream, carries no PID, so the two pathogenic alleles share no read-level phasing and this data cannot show whether they lie on different chromosomes [vep:7:117559590:ATCT:A] [vep:7:117587778:G:T]. Two ClinVar-pathogenic alleles of one recessive gene in a proband with the phenotype make trans the likelier configuration, but only parental genotypes or long-read phasing can show it.

criteria.justification: In-frame deletion of one residue (Phe508, protein position 507-508, exon 11/27 of the MANE transcript NM_000492.4) in the NBD1 domain, not a repeat region
Detected with a second ClinVar-pathogenic CFTR allele, p.Gly542Ter, in the same proband; the two share no physical-phasing group (28.2 kb apart), so phase is unknown rather than shown to be cis

[RETIRED — PP5 is retired (retired by the ClinGen SVI (Biesecker & Harrison 2018): accepted for the record, marked, never counted); the ClinVar classification is concordance, not a criterion] ClinVar Pathogenic, practice guideline (4 stars), for cystic fibrosis

The case terms (elevated sweat chloride, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, recurrent respiratory infections, chronic lung disease, bronchiectasis) are the classic cystic fibrosis picture, a single-gene CFTR disorder
gnomAD v4 af 0.0119 (19237 of 1612320 alleles) with 58 homozygotes: not absent; the carrier frequency of the commonest CF allele, not evidence against it

variants.summary: Heterozygous p.Phe508del (0/1, AD 23,19), the commonest cystic fibrosis allele: an in-frame single-residue deletion in NBD1, ClinVar Pathogenic at practice-guideline level [vep:7:117559590:ATCT:A] [clinvar:VCV000007105]; its gnomAD frequency and 58 homozygotes reflect a recessive allele at carrier frequency, not benignity [gnomad:7-117559590-ATCT-A].

criteria.justification: Nonsense p.Gly542Ter (stop_gained, HIGH) in exon 12/27 of the MANE transcript NM_000492.4, far upstream of the last exon junction, so nonsense-mediated decay is predicted; loss of function is the established mechanism of cystic fibrosis
Detected with p.Phe508del, a second ClinVar-pathogenic CFTR allele, in the same proband; no shared physical-phasing group, so phase is unknown rather than shown to be cis

what_would_change_the_call: Parental genotypes or long-read phasing showing the two alleles in cis would remove PM3 from both
A sweat chloride measurement or a CFTR functional assay on the proband's cells
A revised ClinVar assertion or a gnomAD release with homozygotes for p.Gly542Ter
